editorial:
Imagine moving your family into a big, old house only to find out the previous owner was a creepy occultist. That is exactly what happens to Dr. Norman Boyle. He thinks he is getting a great deal on a Boston mansion, but the place is actually built on a graveyard. The vibe is super spooky from the start, especially when his young son begins seeing a ghost girl who tries to warn him that something evil is hiding in the walls. It feels like a classic nightmare where you know something is wrong, but the adults just refuse to listen until it is too late.

You will notice that the plot is a bit messy and some of the acting feels stiff, but that is part of the charm. The gore is over-the-top and looks very realistic for the early 80s, which makes the scary parts really pop. If you love old-school horror that does not explain everything, you will have a blast.
endingExplained: You find out that the house is actually a gateway to hell. The ghost girl is trying to stop the evil spirit from taking over. In the end, the house literally opens up and swallows the family. Everything collapses into a giant pit of fire and monsters. There is no happy ending here; the family is dragged down into the ground, and the house disappears, leaving nothing behind but a wasteland.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s Italian horror and gross special effects.
